title: feat(spec, plugin-audit): a sealed object names its chain column with lifecycle.seal.chainField
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
Fixes #34164

_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbSUQWB2j9eHYsRcrCiq1X1C)_

Clause-②: yes (widening). A sealed object may name its chain column with `lifecycle.seal.chainField`; the default stays `tenant_id`, and an object that seals today is byte-identical.
Metadata-protocol: added
Skills-docs: follow-up #33773

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:审计封存对象可以用 `lifecycle.seal.chainField` 指定按哪一列分组织成链(默认仍是 `tenant_id`);封存器、`os audit verify` 现场校验和证明包统一经一个函数读取链值。编写期拒绝点名的列:对象没有的列、取值不是文本的列(数字、布尔、日期、日期时间、JSON、多值)、`id`/`created_at`、以及同时列在 `valueFields` 里的列。既无 `tenant_id` 又没写 `chainField` 的对象仍可通过编写,由封存器报错且不封存(这一半是 #34352)。
- 为什么改:企业版的 AI 审计日志 `sys_ai_audit_log` 的组织在平台注入的 `organization_id` 列里,没有 `tenant_id`,今天根本无法封存;cloud#4128 等这条框架接缝。
- 风险与回滚:默认 `tenant_id` 的对象叶子输入、签名体、根逐字节不变(有基线摘要钉住);新键可选,新增的拒绝都只针对新键,主干上能解析的声明一条也不多拒。已有检查点的对象改 `chainField` 会让校验失败(已实测并写进文档)。回滚即撤掉本 PR。含 ADR-0154 附注,属 Tier H 面。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`(`refuseUnknownSealChainField` 的四种拒绝与 `nonTextChainColumnType`)、`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts`(五处读链改走 `chainValueOf`)、ADR-0154 文末附注。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/data/object-lifecycle-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts`,预期 25 条全绿:数字、日期、JSON、多值列以及 `id`、与 `valueFields` 重叠的列都在 `lifecycle.seal.chainField` 处被拒,文本与 lookup 列照常通过。
- 需要你做的:审阅并合并(含 `docs/adr/**`,需维护者批准)。

## What changes

- **`@objectstack/spec`.** `lifecycle.seal` gains the optional `chainField`: the column whose value is the organization chain a sealed row joins. `refuseUnknownSealChainField` refuses a NAMED column, each time with one located issue at `lifecycle.seal.chainField`:
  - a column the object does not have. Declared fields count, and so do the columns the registry injects (`resolveInjectedSystemColumns`): `organization_id` counts unless the object opts out of the tenant column;
  - (round 3, review S1) a column whose value is not one text on every store. The set is derived, not listed: `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES`, `BOOLEAN_VALUE_TYPES`, `CALENDAR_DATE_TYPES`, `INSTANT_TYPES` and `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` from the field-value contract, plus any field `isMultiValueField` calls multi-value. A declared column is judged by its own definition; an injected one by the definition the registry injects (`injectedSystemColumnDefs`), so the injected `updated_at` (a `datetime`) is refused. `chainValueOf` reads a chain only from a non-empty string, so such a column would put rows into the deployment chain with no report;
  - (round 3, review S1) `id` and `created_at`, through `isSealLeafOrderColumn`, the predicate the `valueFields` refusal now reads too (extracted from its inline check, same two names);
  - (round 3, review S2) a column `valueFields` also lists: the leaf would commit the value while the chain carries it in clear in every checkpoint and proof bundle.
  The default case, an object that names no `chainField`, is not judged at authoring: that half is #34352. The reference docs regenerate.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-audit`.** One reader, `chainValueOf(row, chainField)`, with `sealChainFieldOf(lifecycle)` for the default, both in `audit-seal/canonical.ts`. It replaces the sealer's and the verifier's `tenantOf`. The sealer reads it at its five chain reads; the live check reads it for rows no checkpoint holds, which is also where the proof bundle's `unsealed` entries come from. The checkpoint's signed `tenant_id` member keeps its name and carries the chain value. No source change in round 3.
- **ADR-0154.** One note, appended. Round 3: its status cites hand-off 6912069272 (the 09:00Z ruling) and #34352, and says an object with neither column still parses and is reported by the sealer (S4); D10 records the round-3 refusals and that the chain column is fixed once the object has checkpoints, with what a change costs, measured (S1, S2, S3); D5, D10 and the "Names this record fixes" row each gain a dated pointer to the note (N1).
- **`os audit verify`.** No source change: `--org` passes through as `orgs` to the live check, which reads the chain column.
- **Docs.** `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` § Sealed audit objects teaches `chainField`: its default, every name authoring refuses (round 3 adds the non-text, leaf-order and `valueFields` refusals), that an object with neither column still parses and is reported, the empty-value rule, `--org`, and (round 3) that the chain column is fixed once the object has checkpoints. The changeset says the same.

## Tests

- `packages/spec/src/data/object-lifecycle-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` (25 tests): the key parses for the injected `organization_id`, a declared field, and (round 3 control) a declared `text`, `lookup` and `select` column. A seal without the key is unchanged. Refused at the key, each asserted by code, path and the message's first sentence: an unknown name, an undeclared `tenant_id`, `organization_id` under the three tenant opt-outs; (round 3) a declared `number`, `currency`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `json` and `multiselect` column, a `lookup` declared `multiple: true`, the injected `updated_at`; `id` and `created_at` declared, and `id` only the driver provides; a chain column also in `valueFields`, declared or the injected `organization_id`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/audit-seal-chain-field-34164.test.ts` (52 tests):
  - Live `ObjectKernel` over SQLite: one chain per organization by the injected `organization_id`; `verifyAuditLedger({ orgs: ['org_x'] })` reports only org_x; a row edited below the hooks reads `modified` in its own chain.
  - Byte identity against digests from the base sealer, for the default and for `chainField: 'tenant_id'`.
  - A definition that skipped the parse and names a column it lacks is not sealed, and is reported at `error`.
  - (round 3) For every `FieldType` with a canonical rule, the spec refuses it as a chain column exactly when the sealer's own rule (`AUDIT_SEAL_TYPE_RULES`) is not `text`; `select`, `radio`, `lookup` and `user` with `multiple: true` are refused. This holds the derived spec set to the reader's rules.
  - (round 3, S3, measured) On the in-memory store, an object sealed by `tenant_id` and then switched to `chainField: 'org_ref'`: the next pass seals the last sealed window's row again under the new chain (checkpoints `org:org_a window r1`, `org:org_a window r2`, then `org:org_b window r2`, `org:org_b window r3`); the whole check reports `org:org_b#0:listed_twice` and is not ok; scoped to `org_b`, the row sealed earlier reads `late`, unsealed, and the check is not ok.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/audit/verify.chain-field-34164.integration.test.ts`: unchanged in round 3 (the real command, spawned, `--org org_x` / `--org org_y`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Option A, by the seat's shape ruling (hand-off 6912069272).** Authoring judges only a NAMED `chainField`. An object that names none and has no `tenant_id` still parses, and the sealer still reports it at `error` and does not seal it. Refusing that case, and a non-text `tenant_id`, at parse would refuse declarations that parse today; that half is #34352. The sealer-time check stays for definitions that skip the parse.
- **Every round-3 refusal needs the new key, so none narrows.** `lifecycle.seal` is a strict object: on `main` any `chainField` is refused as an unknown key. Each added refusal fires only when `chainField` is present, so nothing that parses on `main` is refused here, and `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: added` hold.
- **How the non-text set was derived.** From the field-value classes (ADR-0104 D1) and from what `chainValueOf` accepts (a non-empty string): numbers and booleans are never strings; `date` / `datetime` and JSON payloads are text on one store and a `Date` or parsed value on another, which is why the sealer gives them their own canonical rules. `time` stays allowed (its stored form is always `HH:MM` text, sealer rule `text`). Types with no canonical rule (`password`, `secret`, `formula`, the file types) are not judged as chain columns: the sealer does not seal an object that declares one. The plugin-audit cross-check above pins the agreement per type.
- **A definition that skipped the parse with a non-text chain column** still seals its rows into the deployment chain, as a non-text `tenant_id` does on `main` today; the sealer has no type check for the chain column. Noted, not built: the default half belongs with #34352.
- **An import cycle, deliberate and function-only.** `object.zod.ts` imports `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` and now `injectedSystemColumnDefs`; both modules import `isTenancyDisabled` back from `object.zod.ts` (the second through the first). Each side calls the other only at parse time. The field-value sets are read inside a function too, never at module evaluation, since `field-value.zod` sits in the `field.zod` evaluation cycle.
- **Loose ends.** "A `chainField` also listed in `valueFields`" is now refused (S2). The platform-global deployment case stays accepted as shipped, per the review's ①: a `chainField: 'organization_id'` passes authoring, and the sealer reports that object at `error` and does not seal it.
- **Not taken from the review:** N2 (`sealChainFieldOf` answers `tenant_id` for an empty or non-string `chainField` on a definition that skipped the parse) and N3 (`sys_audit_checkpoint.chain_key` is sized for an organization id).
- **Skills still to teach the key:** `skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md` § Sealing and the stale verifier claim in `skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` go to #33773 (the `Skills-docs:` line). `skills/**` is not touched here.
